personality.description: This person tends to stick to familiar routines, rely on proven methods, and feel uneasy when asked to embrace unfamiliar ideas. They are often spontaneous and loosely organized, which can make them miss deadlines or leave plans unfinished, yet they adapt quickly when circumstances change. In moral dilemmas, they usually judge situations through a skeptical, self-protective lens, weighing personal advantage first and questioning others’ intentions before conceding ground. In group discussions, they speak briefly and cautiously, prefer smaller and quieter settings, and may sound guarded, direct, and somewhat resistant to compromise; stress can make them more tense, but they usually regain composure without much difficulty.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
